svg.text: VERSION CONTROL — CLASS DESIGN (LLD)
THE REPOSITORY — orchestrator over four collaborators
Repository
final class · VersionControl is a thin ctor wrapper around it
objectStore · commitStore · branchManager · mergeStrategy
currentBranch: String — HEAD, as a branch NAME
workingDirectory: HashMap<path, content>
commitCounter: int — ids are c001, c002, ...
addFile(path, content) · deleteFile(path)
commit(message, author): Commit — throws if the diff is empty
status(): Diff · diff(fromId, toId): Diff · log(): List<Commit>
createBranch(name) · checkout(name) · merge(name)
discardChanges() · head(): Commit
requireCleanWorkingDirectory(op) — private guard
checkout AND merge both refuse to run with a dirty working dir —
one guard, two call sites, and no silent data loss ✓
the ctor seeds an empty tree + "initial commit" + branch main ✓
THERE IS NO STAGING AREA. addFile writes straight into the
working dir and commit() snapshots ALL of it. No `git add`,
no partial commit — that is the biggest divergence from Git.
Commit ids are a COUNTER, not a content hash. Only blobs and
trees are content-addressed here.
THE SEAMS — three interfaces, one that got away
«interface» CommitStore
save(commit) · get(id) · contains(id)
log(fromId): List<Commit>
isAncestor(ancestorId, descendantId): boolean
isAncestor is the reachability query the whole merge rests on
InMemoryCommitStore: HashMap + iterative DFS over parents
«interface» BranchManager
create(name, commitId) — throws if the name exists
get(name) · exists(name) · getAll(): Map
advance(branchName, commitId)
a branch is JUST a movable pointer — advance() is the whole idea ✓
«interface» MergeStrategy
merge(ourHead, theirHead, commitStore, objectStore): Commit
STRATEGY — swap 3-way for ours / theirs / octopus / rebase
both stores are passed IN, so a strategy stays stateless ✓
ObjectStore is a CONCRETE class — the one collaborator with no seam
CONTENT ADDRESSING — the part that is real Git
ObjectStore — the content-addressed heap
blobs: HashMap<sha1, Blob> · trees: HashMap<sha1, Tree>
storeBlob(content): String — key IS the hash, so a repeat store is a no-op
storeTree(Map<path, content>): String — stores every blob, then the tree
resolveFiles(treeHash): Map<path, content> — the read path
DEDUP FOR FREE: an unchanged file across 100 commits is ONE Blob ✓
an unchanged DIRECTORY is one Tree — same hash, same object ✓
nothing is ever deleted: no GC, no packfiles, no reachability sweep.
Blob · Tree
Blob: content + sha1(content) — immutable
Tree: entries Map<path, blobHash>, unmodifiable
Tree hash = sha1 over a CANONICAL form:
"tree" + for each sorted entry: path \0 blobHash \n
TreeMap sort makes the hash order-independent —
same files in, same hash out, every time ✓
Tree is FLAT: paths are strings, not nested trees.
SHA-1, not SHA-256 — fine here, not for security.
Commit · Branch · Diff
Commit: id, message, author, timestamp,
parentIds: List<String>, treeHash — all final
getFiles(store) → resolveFiles(treeHash)
Branch: name (final) + commitId (MUTABLE)
Diff: List<Change> of ADD / MODIFY / DELETE
parentIds is a LIST ⇒ a merge commit has two ✓
Diff is FILE-level. Two versions of a file are either
equal or MODIFY — no line-level LCS anywhere.
objectStore (concrete — no interface)
reads/writes
THE MERGE MACHINERY
MergeBaseFinder — static utility
findMergeBase(store, a, b): String
1. collect ALL ancestors of A into a HashSet (BFS)
2. BFS outward from B; first id found in that set wins
private ctor — it holds no state, so it is a function, not an object ✓
"first hit in BFS order" is the NEAREST common ancestor by hop
count from B — not necessarily the unique best base in a
criss-cross history. Git runs a proper LCA and can recurse.
Returns null for unrelated histories — merge treats base as empty.
SimpleMerge implements MergeStrategy
same commit ⇒ throw "already up to date"
isAncestor(ours, theirs) ⇒ FAST-FORWARD: return theirHead
isAncestor(theirs, ours) ⇒ throw "already up to date"
otherwise ⇒ 3-way over base ∪ ours ∪ theirs paths
fast-forward creates NO new commit — it just moves the pointer ✓
a conflict THROWS IllegalStateException listing the paths. There is
no MERGING state, no conflict markers, no resolve step — the whole
merge is abandoned and the working dir is left untouched.

g.text: WHY CONTENT ADDRESSING?
A commit does not store files. It
stores ONE tree hash. The tree maps
paths to blob hashes. The blob is
keyed by the hash of its own bytes.
So identical content is stored once,
no matter how many commits or
branches reference it.
Dedup is a side effect of the key.
THREAD SAFETY: THERE IS NONE
Every map in this design is a plain HashMap —
objects, commits, branches, working directory.
Nothing is synchronized anywhere.
That is the right call: a working copy belongs to
one developer, and real Git serialises with an
index.lock FILE rather than in-process locks.
If asked to make it a SERVER: the object store is
append-only and safe; branch advance needs a CAS.

svg.text: WHITEBOARD ORDER:
① Repository + working directory → ② the three seams (CommitStore / BranchManager / MergeStrategy) → ③ ObjectStore: content → Blob → Tree → Commit → ④ merge base + 3-way — then name the missing index
LEGEND
